title: Cross-Lane Message Envelope
description: One durable, at-least-once-delivered message between lanes, written as a file under queue/inbox/<ts>-<uuid>.json and drained by atomic rename through queue/processing/ to queue/done/. Exists because a run record read 'bastion:BA.21.A is now unblocked on the engine side' only by a human noticing it in prose, never signalled, so the waiting lane idled; because the corpus's one real cross-lane ping (base-template/planning/orchestration-run/autonomous-foundation/notes.md, 2026-08-21) had no typed carrier; because a rendezvous need ('the D62 downstream check against bastion is DEFERRED until this lane is idle') had no primitive to express it; and because the four sweep incidents behind BT.6.A (lease.schema.json) need a durable RELEASE signal, not just a durable claim. This schema deliberately carries NO priority or urgency property: a sender-declared priority inflates to always-urgent and forks a second rubric alongside D43, which owns priority in this fleet. Sibling to lane-agent.schema.json and lease.schema.json. This block ships the envelope shape only; sending, receiving, responding and draining are BT.6.C and BT.6.D.

message_id.description: The uuid half of the message's filename stem (queue/inbox/<ts>-<uuid>.json), duplicated here so a drain can assert exactly-once delivery by identity rather than by path. A filename whose uuid half disagrees with this value is an error.

sender.description: The BT.6.A registry key (lane-agent.schema.json's agent_name/repo/lane/roadmap) identifying who sent this message, so a receiver can address a reply without calling ListAgents.

agent_name.description: The ListAgents nickname the sender was reachable at when this message was sent, matching lane-agent.schema.json's agent_name.

repo.description: Repo slug the sending lane is driving, as registered in brain.toml.

lane.description: The sending lane's name/slug, matching the <name> in its lane-<name>.json record.

roadmap.description: Slug of the roadmap directory the sending lane runs under.

sent_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp with timezone marking when this message was written to the inbox.

kind.description: Exactly five kinds, each derived from a measured incident, no others: EDGE_RELEASED (a dependency edge is now clear on the sender's side and the receiver's lane may have been idling on it, unsignalled, as in the bastion:BA.21.A incident); FINDING (a cross-lane observation worth relaying, the corpus's one measured real-world case); RENDEZVOUS (a need for two lanes to synchronize before either proceeds, e.g. a downstream check deferred until a sibling lane goes idle); LEASE_RELEASE (one kind covering both taking and releasing a repo lease per lease.schema.json, discriminated in the body — kept as one kind, not two, so the enum stays at exactly five); QUERY (a read-only question that implies no action by the receiver, kept separate so questions are never dressed up as findings). Drain-routing rule (consumed by BT.6.D, stated here next to the kinds it discriminates): RENDEZVOUS and LEASE_RELEASE may trigger an immediate drain on their kind alone, because they concern the tree and are objectively time-critical; FINDING never triggers a drain.

subject.description: What this message is about: the subject block or repo, per the block record. block is optional because some messages (e.g. a repo-wide RENDEZVOUS) are not about any single block.

repo.description: Repo slug this message concerns, as registered in brain.toml.

block.description: Optional block id this message concerns (e.g. 'BT.6.A'), when the message is about a specific block rather than the repo as a whole.

body.description: The message content itself. Free text; for LEASE_RELEASE this is where taking vs releasing is discriminated.

durable_home.description: Names where the same item was already, or is about to be, written to disk (lane log, state.json edge, or carryover slug), so that a lost message is never a lost item — the message is a signal about durable state, not the durable state itself.

channel.description: Which durable-record kind holds this item.

ref.description: A locator within that channel (e.g. a lane-log line id, a state.json edge slug, a carryover slug, or a run-record path) precise enough for a receiver to go find the durable item itself.
